chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام amputated the hand of a man for a baydah.”
I said, “And what kind of baydah?” He said, “An iron helmet, the value of which was one-third of a dinar.”
So I said, “This is the minimum limit for the thief.” Then he remained silent.

key_terms.أَدْنَى حَدِّ السَّارِقِ: the minimum threshold at which the thief’s hadd applies
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, identified as the authority who applied the ruling
key_terms.بَيْضَةٍ: an iron helmet mentioned as the stolen item
key_terms.ثُلُثُ دِينَارٍ: one-third of a dinar, the amount stated in the report
key_terms.حَدِيدٍ: iron, specifying the material of the helmet
key_terms.قَطَعَ: carried out amputation as the legal hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value at which the hadd punishment for theft applies in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام carried out the hadd punishment for theft involving an iron helmet valued at one-third of a dinar. The narration indicates that this amount represents the minimum threshold for the thief’s hadd, as implied by the questioner’s statement and the Imam’s silence.
